summary.intent: Land a stacked series of Callisto fixes so unreadable or malformed files and manifests are reported as errors rather than silently treated as missing or as 'admit everything'. PR 1 (strict reads) is shipped; PR 2 (discovery-total) makes membership, workspace-root lookup and symlinked-package handling total and typed.
summary.outcome: Opened PR #235 (fix/strict-reads) and started an independent review. On a new fix/discovery-total worktree stacked on it, `OpenContext::for_workspace_root` now returns a Result with all callers updated, membership.rs was rewritten with typed errors, find_workspace_root no longer walks past a malformed manifest, and symlinked-package rejection was added. The work was committed as a WIP with membership tests still mid-flip.

repo: Callisto is a Rust workspace with crates callisto-graph, callisto-manifests and others; clippy is run with `--all-targets -- -D warnings` and must be clean workspace-wide.
Discovery code lives in crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ (membership.rs, root.rs, ignore_walk.rs, mod.rs).

Several old membership/root tests pinned an unsafe fallback (malformed input admits everything or walks past to a different root), so they must be flipped to expect errors, not only patched with `.unwrap()`.
membership.rs has npm production code sitting between two test modules, so regex-based test rewrites over the file can hit production code.

code.finding: Defines `OpenContext::for_workspace_root`, which was changed to return a Result. Callers are in callisto-graph (apply.rs, commands/init.rs, commands/matrix.rs, commands/version.rs, lib.rs, walk.rs) and in the cargo_tests.rs and ecosystem_bugs_test.rs tests.
Rewritten so malformed input becomes a typed error. A valid file with no restriction is now the only way to get 'admit everything'.
`find_workspace_root` used to walk past a malformed manifest to a different root. It was changed to stop and report the malformed manifest.

workflow: Large mechanical refactors were done with throwaway Python scripts in the scratchpad, run with `python3 -I`, then verified with clippy and targeted `cargo test` filters.
Stacked PRs use a git worktree branched from the previous PR's branch, so PR 2 can proceed while PR 1 is under review.
A WIP commit with `--no-verify` checkpoints a mid-flip state before switching context.
The independent reviewer was spawned without cargo, so it reviews by reading rather than building.

friction: The regex-based test rewrite in member_tests.py also hit the npm production code between two test modules in membership.rs, and that definition had to be reverted by hand.
Flipping the membership tests is a two-way job: mechanical `.unwrap()` for valid cases plus semantic flips where tests pinned the unsafe fallback. It was scripted, but not all of it was finished.
open_items: Finish flipping the membership/root/symlink tests; the WIP commit says tests are mid-flip.
Re-run the full workspace test suite and clippy after the test flips, then clean up the WIP commit before opening the PR 2 (discovery-total) PR.
Handle the independent review result for PR #235 once it returns.
Rebase or retarget PR 2 once PR #235 merges.
